item.title: PwC International Can’t Exit Evergrande Case, HK Court Rules
item.description: Deputy High Court Judge Patrick Fung said the evidence PwC International submitted as part of its arguments to exit the case was “inadequate and unsatisfactory,” according to a judgment delivered on Wednesday. A Hong Kong court declined to remove PricewaterhouseCoopers International Ltd. The case centers on PwC’s auditing work for Evergrande, an emblem of China’s property crisis since it defaulted in 2021.

item.description: As a result of these changes, Michelle Bain, Executive General Manager of Compulsory Third Party Insurance, will join the Executive Leadership Team as Suncorp’s Chief Risk Officer. Australian insurer Suncorp has announced a number of new executive leadership appointments, including Bridget Messer as Chief Executive Customer, Brand and Digital, a newly created role. item.title: Nearmap launches itel Total Price for guaranteed whole-home property claims pricing
item.description: Nearmap, a property intelligence provider, has launched itel Total Price, a new whole-home pricing solution designed to provide guaranteed pricing for major exterior and interior building materials across property claims, with the solution now available within Verisk Xactimate®. “itel Total Price gives carriers a single trusted source for guaranteed pricing across the entire home, helping improve claim outcomes within the trusted Verisk Xactimate(R) platform.” Nearmap said the pricing database underpinning itel Total Price draws on more than 30 years of proprietary materials intelligence and historical pricing data from more than 15 million claims. Nearmap’s itel Total Price provides pricing backed by fulfilment, with the company positioning the solution as a way for insurers to manage material costs throughout the claims process.

item.title: Western Wildland Firefighters Warned About Supplement for Smoke Exposure
item.description: Fire and medical officials have issued warnings about a supplement offered to Western wildland firefighters who have been exposed to toxic chemicals while battling some of the country’s biggest blazes. Though there is no evidence to back its use, some firefighters have said the supplement helped them feel better after breathing toxic smoke and they have urged California pharmacy officials not to restrict access. The supplement glutathione, given through an IV or an inhaler-like machine called a nebulizer, has not been proven to be safe or effective and could expose firefighters to illness if there is contamination while it’s produced, experts say.

item.title: Near-Miss Data Can Expedite Self-Driving Vehicle Algorithm Training: Study
item.description: Rather than relying on the vast amounts of routine driving data typically used to train autonomous systems, the method focuses on “near-miss” scenarios—rare but safety-critical events that challenge vehicle decision-making. Researchers have developed a new approach to boosting self-driving vehicle algorithms that could significantly reduce the time and cost required to prepare automated vehicles for real-world deployment, according to the University of Michigan. The team tested their approach, incorporating both safety-critical and near-miss scenarios, achieving a 90% improvement in the vehicle’s safety performance.

item.title: Marsh to bring alternative capital into data centre risks with $10bn Stratus exchange
item.description: Broker Marsh is aiming to bring alternative sources of insurance and reinsurance capital into the digital infrastructure risk transfer sector, through the launch of a $10 billion property insurance exchange named Stratus. Marsh is clearly seeking to bring alternative and third-party capital in to help fill this gap through this new Stratus insurance exchange. Stratus offers access up to $10 billion in property insurance capacity on a single-placement basis, Marsh explained, with this targeted at the complex operational risks of digital infrastructure projects, including data centers and related critical support systems.

item.title: Brian Botkin promoted to International CUO for MS&AD
item.description: MSIG USA has announced the promotion of Brian Botkin to International Chief Underwriting Officer for MS&AD Insurance Group. Botkin has served as MSIG USA’s Chief Underwriting Officer since July 2024, playing a key role in the firm’s transformation and growth by leading enterprise underwriting strategy and advancing greater consistency, discipline and portfolio insight across the organisation. In his new role, Botkin will leverage that experience across MS&AD’s global operations, helping advance underwriting strategy, governance and portfolio management across markets.

item.title: Solid capital and annuity demand fuels global life & annuity reinsurers’ growth: AM Best
item.description: The report, titled “Global Life/Annuity Reinsurers Remained Poised for Steady Growth,” comes ahead of the annual Rendez-Vous de Septembre in Monte Carlo, as primary carriers lean heavily on reinsurers to navigate higher interest rates, strong annuity product growth, and further offshore transactions as a result of differing capital regimes. The global life and annuity (L/A) reinsurance market remains well capitalised and positioned for sustained expansion, driven by increased dedicated capital for traditional life coverage and a surge in third-party backing for asset-intensive annuity business, according to a new report by AM Best. “The treatment of required capital and reserves is often less stringent than for reinsurers domiciled onshore in the United States,” said Edward Kohlberg, director, AM Best.

item.description: The world’s top container shipper MSC Mediterranean Shipping Co. MSC said it’s closely monitoring the situation, and customers are being advised to contact its Russia agency for possible logistics alternatives for imports and exports until conditions allow the resumption of regular weekly services from the Black Sea port. item.title: Meta to Pay Texas $1 Billon in Child Safety Case
item.description: Social media giant Meta will pay over $1 billion to Texas and implement sweeping protections for children as part of a settlement with the state, Attorney General Ken Paxton announced Wednesday. The settlement comes as Meta, the company behind Facebook and Instagram, tentatively agreed to a $17 billion payout to resolve a separate lawsuit brought by 33 states, which Texas was not a part of. As part of Texas’ settlement, Meta will apply stricter age verification measures and institute a daily two-hour limit for teens.

item.title: Some Gary, Indiana Residents Still Without Power Weeks After Storms
item.description: “No outage is being overlooked, and no customer will be left behind as we continue this restoration effort.” As the Indiana residents awaited restoration of their service, roughly 34,000 customers in the majority Black city of Memphis were still without power as of late Monday afternoon, after storms swept through the city on Saturday, according to information on Memphis Light, Gas and Water’s website. Things became all-too familiar for Kimya Williams after storms rumbled through Gary, Indiana, earlier this month leaving big chunks of the mostly-Black city in the dark for two weeks. The day before, Gary Mayor Eddie Melton called the pace of restoration “unacceptable.” “We’re at day 12 and 12 days is too long for families to be without power, 12 days is too long for parents to worry about their children and for businesses to lose revenue,” Melton said in an update to the community.

item.title: VIG reports 21% profit rise in H1 2026 to €641.5m
item.description: Vienna Insurance Group (VIG) has reported a 20.7% rise in result before taxes to €641.5m for the first half of 2026, driven primarily by a strong total capital investment result and an improved net combined ratio. Insurance service revenue rose 7.1% to €6.85bn, supported by growth in life insurance without profit participation of 18.2%, unit and index-linked life insurance of 10.7%, and health insurance of 8.8%. Gross written premiums reached €9.03bn, a year-on-year increase of 5.4%, with the strongest growth again in life insurance without profit participation, at 18.4%.

item.title: AI financial infrastructure firm Corgi launches admitted insurance carrier
item.description: AI financial infrastructure firm Corgi has launched an admitted insurance carrier, adding to the range of insurance structures it already operates across its group, including risk retention groups, reinsurers, captives, and managing general agencies. The launch of admitted carrier Corgi Insurance Company expands the range of options the group can deploy for a given account. Emily Yuan, co-founder and chief operating officer of Corgi, said the carrier was part of the firm’s wider ambitions.

item.title: Heffernan acquires Kristin Manwaring Insurance Associates
item.description: Heffernan Insurance has acquired the assets of Kristin Manwaring Insurance Associates, an independent insurance agency based in Port Townsend, Washington. Kristin Manwaring and her team joined Heffernan effective May 1. Founded in 1988 and headquartered in Walnut Creek, California, Heffernan offers business and personal insurance, employee benefits, and financial services.

item.title: Hagerty appoints insurance transformation executive
item.description: Hagerty has appointed Greg Cicero as vice president of insurance transformation. At Hagerty, Cicero will help lead the implementation of Apex, the company’s new policy administration system, working across its insurance and technology teams to modernize core operations and improve the policy lifecycle. Cicero joins after nearly 22 years at Progressive, where he most recently served as customer IT platform owner and led a 110-person organization responsible for customer systems, including identity management, data warehouses, AI systems and marketing technology.

item.title: Vanguard to acquire Altruist
item.description: Vanguard has entered into an agreement to acquire Altruist , a wealth technology and custody platform serving registered investment advisors. item.title: FCA bans trio behind £35.5m scheme designed to bypass visa rules
item.description: The FCA has decided to ban 3 former senior figures at Dolfin Financial (UK) Limited (Dolfin) after finding they ran a scheme that helped clients bypass UK visa rules. These individuals ran a scheme designed to get around the UK's investor visa rules, undermining their purpose of attracting genuine investment into the UK. Between 2016 and 2019, most clients using the scheme paid a fee of £400,000 instead of investing £2m of their own money in UK companies, as required under the Home Office investor visa rules.

So far this year, legal tech startups have pulled in more than $2.2 billion.

item.title: Third-party capital around one-third of global life annuity reinsurance capacity: AM Best & GC
item.description: In a new report this morning, rating agency AM Best highlights the expansive global life and annuity reinsurance space saying it is “well capitalized and positioned for robust growth due to increased dedicated capital for life reinsurance for traditional life business and more asset-intensive annuity business via third-party capital.” After which it provides the estimate from the reinsurance broker, writing, “Guy Carpenter estimates that third-party capital accounted for around one-third of total capacity in 2025, which has doubled since 2022.” Which drives home the increasingly important role of third-party capital structures in the life and annuity reinsurance market around the world. As use of third-party capital within life annuity reinsurance structures including sidecar vehicles increases, a new estimate from reinsurance broker Guy Carpenter, as reported by rating agency AM Best, suggests around one-third of capacity is now from third-party investor sources. In fact, this shows that third-party capital penetration into the life and annuities market has been far more rapid than in P&C reinsurance risks, where alternative or ILS capital from third-party investors remains around 18% of global dedicated reinsurance capital, according to recent data from the same pair of companies .

item.title: EIB and WFP launch parametric insurance scheme to protect Ethiopian smallholder farmers
item.description: The European Investment Bank (EIB), through its development arm EIB Global, is issuing a grant of up to €4 million to the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), which will be used to support the development and rollout of parametric insurance products to protect smallholder farmers in Ethiopia. WFP will use its extensive expertise in rural finance and climate-resilience programming in Ethiopia to develop and pilot this index-based microinsurance (parametric) scheme in partnership with a number of private insurance companies. The grant will support capacity building for the Development Bank of Ethiopia, rural finance institutions and smallholder farmers, as well as the establishment of a Premium Guarantee Fund to pre-finance insurance premiums.

item.title: Swiss pension Nest says ILS investments achieved “convincing results again” in 2025
item.description: Nest Sammelstiftung, or the Nest Collective Foundation, a Swiss pension that adopts sustainable investment strategies and allocates to insurance-linked securities through a number of ILS managers has reported that its allocation achieved “convincing results” again in 2025. While on ILS specifically, the Nest pension fund explained, “Insurance Linked Securities (ILS) were again able to benefit from attractive risk premiums and achieved convincing results,” through 2025. For full-year 2025, while the investor does not provide a specific return figure for its ILS investments, the pension said the results were “convincing”.

item.title: Reinsurance capital hit record $663bn in 2025 as cat risk budgets fall: AM Best and Guy Carpenter
item.description: The report shows that dedicated reinsurance capital reached USD $663 billion at the end of 2025, according to data from AM Best and reinsurance broker Guy Carpenter, while catastrophe risk budgets continued to fall. AM Best and Guy Carpenter estimate that total dedicated reinsurance capital increased from USD $607 billion at the end of 2024 to USD $663 billion at the end of 2025. The global reinsurance sector is carrying more capital than ever while allocating a smaller proportion of that capital to catastrophe risk, according to new analysis from AM Best, a global credit rating agency and provider of insurance industry data and analysis.

item.title: Strong earnings and capital give carriers more choice as rates soften: Howden Re
item.description: In Howden Re’s latest re/insurer earnings report, Michelle To, Head of Business Intelligence, said that as pricing becomes more competitive, carriers are taking a closer look at where they grow, which areas they prioritise, and how they deploy capital, with greater emphasis now on cycle management. “Strong operating performance, favourable prior-year reserve development and healthy capital positions are giving carriers choices over where to put capital next,” Howden Re said. “The half-year 2026 report looks beyond headline rate movements to assess how earnings, reserves, capital and portfolio decisions can help us prepare for the next phase of the cycle,” Howden Re explained.

item.description: Willis, a WTW business, has announced the appointment of Paul Haas as Senior Director, Business Development, based in Chicago. item.title: SpaceX Plans $100 Billion Louisiana Site in Post-IPO Growth Push
item.description: SpaceX plans to build a new $100 billion launch site for its Starship rocket on the southern coast of Louisiana, enabling the company to expand operations of the behemoth vehicle that’s critical to its future. Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry and SpaceX executives announced the plans on Tuesday, authorizing the company to build a facility across roughly 125,000 acres (about 506 square kilometers) in a coastal area known as Pecan Island. The site will provide SpaceX with a third potential location for launching Starship, which SpaceX primarily builds and launches in South Texas.

item.title: Freestone Acquires Illinois-Based 360 Benefits
item.description: Freestone Insurance Group, a Shore Capital Partners portfolio company, has acquired 360 Benefits, an employee benefits focused brokerage based in Chicago. The transaction furthers Freestone’s Midwest presence and strengthens its existing employee benefits practice. 360 serves privately held, middle-market employers across a broad range of industries, delivering high-touch consultative benefits and risk management solutions.

item.title: INTX extends technology platform as Xitus Re expands run-off operations
item.description: INTX Insurance Software has extended its relationship with Bermuda-based property and casualty runoff reinsurer Xitus Re, with the INTX (Re)Insurance Operating System continuing to support the company as it adds portfolios, transactions, and operations across multiple jurisdictions. According to INTX, the broader deployment is intended to give Xitus a consistent technology foundation as its business develops. A key component of the deployment is INTX Re, the firm’s assumed reinsurance platform.

item.title: Marsh prepares Archer brand
item.description: Marsh McLennan appears to be preparing a new reinsurance and captive-services brand called “Archer by Marsh.” The company filed a US trademark application for the name on August 13, covering reinsurance brokerage and intermediary services, insurance administration, and the formation, structuring, and management of captive insurers and reinsurance vehicles. No public announcement or operational website for Archer by Marsh appears to have been released. Marsh has made corresponding applications outside the US.

item.description: El patrimonio bajo gestión de los planes de pensiones del Sistema Individual se redujo un 0,62% en el mes de julio, hasta un total gestionado en 93.263 millones de euros, según Vdos. Por tipo de entidad, los grupos internacionales han registrado el mayor incremento patrimonial en el mes en términos porcentuales, con un 1,29%.
